title: Pristine Independent Confirmation of Error Certification and Safe Routing

conclusions.confirmation_verdict: On the pristine independent confirmation cohort (seeds >= 1,100,000, unobserved during model selection and threshold calibration), the empirical findings of Phases 1-7 are conclusively confirmed.
conclusions.surrogate_error_scaling: Refined FNO (A3) improves upon M3 (A0), reducing 256x256 overall mean MaxAE from 16.8 K to 12.4 K, and Selective Boundary Jacobi (A4) further reduces it to 8.9 K. However, at 256x256, 36.7% of A4 cases still violate the MaxAE <= 10 K requirement.
conclusions.certificate_failure: Rigorous operator norm bound (P2) and exact barrier bounds reject 100% of queries on the independent cohort, yielding 0.0x surrogate usage and negative speedup (0.61x). Mathematically certified error bounds are incapable of accepting neural operator predictions.
conclusions.residual_estimator_risk: Under the calibrated threshold tau_jac = 3.0 K, P5 achieves 78.3% acceptance at 256x256, but its conditional failure rate (CFR) is 31.9% (Wilson 95% CI: [20.1%, 46.5%]). This completely fails the production safety threshold (zero unsafe acceptances).
conclusions.final_governance_decision: Production promotion of any hybrid neural routing policy based on residual error estimators or certificates must be REJECTED. The system must remain strictly on the frozen R1 direct FVM pipeline.
